item.title: Singapore Calls for Global Action as Shadow Fleet Pressures Strategic Straits
item.description: Singapore has issued its clearest warning yet over the growing presence of sanctioned “shadow fleet” tankers operating near the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, calling for stronger international cooperation as aging vessels exploit legal grey zones just beyond territorial waters.

item.title: Coast Guard Nets 100+ Tons of Cocaine in Eastern Pacific Drug Crackdown
item.description: The U.S. Coast Guard has seized more than 200,000 pounds of cocaine in the Eastern Pacific since launching Operation Pacific Viper in August, marking one of the largest maritime counter-drug efforts in recent years as U.S. forces also intensify operations against trafficking routes at sea.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions Iran’s Shadow Fleet as Nuclear Talks Resume
item.description: The United States has unveiled a sweeping new sanctions package targeting Iran’s shadow fleet, designating vessels, managers, and traders involved in illicit oil and petrochemical exports as Washington presses Tehran on multiple fronts even as nuclear talks resume.

item.title: Iran, U.S. Restart Nuclear Talks in Oman as Tensions Remain High
item.description: Nuclear talks between Iran and the United States held in Oman on Friday were a good beginning and will continue, Iran's foreign minister said, after growing concerns that a failure in the high-stakes negotiations could set off another Middle East war.

item.title: Supertankers Speed Through Strait of Hormuz as Geopolitical Risk Mounts
item.description: Some supertanker operators are speeding up transits through the Strait of Hormuz as U.S.–Iran tensions rise, with VLCCs reaching speeds well above normal levels in one of the world’s most congested and strategically critical waterways.

item.title: Panama President Says ‘Never Again’ to Exclusive Port Concessions After CK Hutchison Ruling
item.description: Panama's Supreme Court nullified CK Hutchison's nearly 30-year contract to operate two strategic canal ports, ruling it violated constitutional provisions. China warned of "heavy prices" while the Hong Kong firm launches arbitration over the $23B deal.

item.title: Labor Department Eases Insurance Rules for U.S. Shipbuilders
item.description: The U.S. Labor Department has issued new guidance easing insurance requirements under the Longshore and Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act, a move aimed at lowering costs for U.S. shipyards and strengthening the domestic maritime industrial base.

item.title: Oil Tankers Hauling Russian Oil Flood East Asia, Racing for Buyers
item.description: More than a dozen tankers carrying 10-12 million barrels of Russian Urals crude are circling Asia seeking buyers after India cut imports under US pressure. Five tankers are signaling 'for orders' status, indicating no confirmed buyers yet.

item.title: Panama Canal Opens Floodgates as Gatun Lake Reservoir Hits Maximum Capacity
item.description: The Panama Canal Authority opened spillways at Gatún Dam after the reservoir reached its maximum operating level, marking a sharp reversal from the drought that restricted canal traffic during the 2023-24 El Niño.

item.title: Trump Iran Tariff Threatens India, Turkey and China Trade
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order enabling tariffs on countries trading with Iran but did not immediately impose duties. The policy threatens major trade relationships with India, Turkey, and China while a US Navy strike group remains deployed.
